text: Christopher Columbus, the original "repackager" of the New World, arrived in 1492 with the audacity to convince Europe that the Americas were merely a new, slightly spicier version of Asia. One must admire his sheer creativity in convincing the masses that what they really needed was a continent they had already heard rumors of, but with a sleek adjective added to its name: "New." It is truly inspiring to see his commitment to 'exploration' by sailing west to find a route to the East, only to stumble upon a landmass that was, essentially, the same thing they already had, but with a significantly higher price tag in terms of indigenous lives and ecological disruption. The audacity to claim discovery of a place already inhabited by millions is a masterclass in marketing, proving that with enough confidence and a good map, you can sell the same old world to a new audience.
